references.text: Isaiah 35:10 links 'life' and 'joy' to God's people, a theme fulfilled in Jesus' claim to be 'the life' and the way to the Father.
Isaiah 43:11 emphasizes that there is only one Savior, paralleling Jesus' statement that no one comes to the Father except through him.
Isaiah 44:6 uses 'I am' as a divine self-declaration, which resonates with Jesus' 'I am' statement in John 14:6.
Psalm 16:11 promises 'the path of life' and 'joy in your presence,' an image that Jesus makes concrete by identifying himself as the way and the life.
Proverbs 14:26 describes fear of the Lord as a 'path to life,' a concept Jesus fulfills by being the way to the Father.
In John 10:9, Jesus calls himself 'the gate' (the way) into salvation and life, a direct precursor to the claim in 14:6 about being the way to the Father.
John 11:25 contains an identical 'I am' statement where Jesus declares himself to be 'the resurrection and the life,' supporting the theme in 14:6.
